### Decision Tree

A decision tree predicts whether a patient has heart disease by splitting
the data into groups based on clinical predictors. At each split, the tree
selects a variable and cutoff that best separates patients with and without
heart disease.

Decision trees can capture nonlinear relationships and interactions between
predictors. However, large trees may overfit the training data.

We use 10-fold cross-validation to select the complexity parameter (`cp`),
which controls the size of the tree. We then prune the tree and evaluate
its performance on the same testing set used for logistic regression and SVM.

```{r tree-setup}
# Load packages needed for tree modeling and evaluation
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(caret)
library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)

# Convert response to a factor for classification
train_tree <- train
test_tree <- test

train_tree$HeartDisease <- as.factor(train_tree$HeartDisease)
test_tree$HeartDisease <- as.factor(test_tree$HeartDisease)
```

```{r tree-fit}
# Fit an initial classification tree
# cp = 0 allows a larger tree before pruning
tree_model <- rpart(
  HeartDisease ~ .,
  data = train_tree,
  method = "class",
  control = rpart.control(cp = 0, xval = 10)
)

# View the cross-validation results
printcp(tree_model)
```

```{r tree-cv-plot, fig.height=4, fig.width=5}
# Plot cross-validation error against tree complexity
plotcp(tree_model)
```

```{r tree-prune}
# Select cp with the lowest cross-validation error
best_cp <- tree_model$cptable[
  which.min(tree_model$cptable[, "xerror"]), "CP"
]

# Prune the tree using the selected cp
tree_final <- prune(tree_model, cp = best_cp)

# View the selected complexity parameter
best_cp
```

```{r tree-plot, fig.height=5, fig.width=8}
# Plot the final pruned decision tree
rpart.plot(
  tree_final,
  type = 2,
  extra = 104,
  fallen.leaves = TRUE,
  main = "Pruned Decision Tree for Heart Disease"
)
```

Next we use the pruned tree to predict heart disease on the testing set.

```{r tree-final}
# Predict probabilities of heart disease
tree_prob <- predict(
  tree_final,
  newdata = test_tree,
  type = "prob"
)[, "1"]

# Classify using a 0.50 probability threshold
tree_pred <- ifelse(tree_prob >= 0.5, 1, 0)

# Convert predictions to a factor
tree_pred <- factor(tree_pred, levels = c(0, 1))

# Create confusion matrix
tree_cm <- confusionMatrix(
  tree_pred,
  test_tree$HeartDisease,
  positive = "1"
)

# Calculate ROC curve
tree_roc <- roc(
  test_tree$HeartDisease,
  tree_prob,
  levels = c("0", "1"),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

# View confusion matrix
tree_cm$table
```

```{r tree-results}
# Summarize model performance
tree_results <- data.frame(
  Model       = "Decision Tree",
  Accuracy    = round(tree_cm$overall["Accuracy"], 3),
  Sensitivity = round(tree_cm$byClass["Sensitivity"], 3),
  Specificity = round(tree_cm$byClass["Specificity"], 3),
  AUC         = round(as.numeric(auc(tree_roc)), 3)
)

# Include the same baseline as the other models
baseline <- data.frame(
  Model       = "Baseline (always 'disease')",
  Accuracy    = round(mean(test_tree$HeartDisease == "1"), 3),
  Sensitivity = 1,
  Specificity = 0,
  AUC         = 0.5
)

tree_results <- rbind(baseline, tree_results)
rownames(tree_results) <- NULL

tree_results
```

```{r tree-roc, fig.height=4, fig.width=5}
# Plot decision tree ROC curve
ggroc(tree_roc, legacy.axes = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey") +
  labs(
    title = "Decision Tree ROC Curve (Test Set)",
    x = "1 - Specificity",
    y = "Sensitivity"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r tree-export}
# Save predictions for the "Comparing Results" section
tree_test_probs <- data.frame(
  actual = test_tree$HeartDisease,
  tree = tree_prob
)
```
